title: Edge OTLP preprocessor: model-shape tagging and cardinality hygiene
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: In production we see explosions in metric cardinality coming from inference edge collectors. Per-request attributes (prompt_hash, raw_route, sequence_text_size) are leaking into Prometheus labels and increasing memory/TSDB churn. This causes high remote_write latency and expensive series churn for tenant dashboards. Goal: implement a lightweight OTLP preprocessor that runs in the edge aggregator (sidecar or daemonset) which canonicalizes and tags OTLP Metric/Span payloads with low-cardinality 'model_shape' and 'route_class' labels and performs safe label redaction and collapse before forwarding to the central telemetry fabric.

Proposed solution: build an extensible preprocessor implemented as a Go service that accepts OTLP/gRPC (and OTLP/HTTP) and performs the following pipeline: 1) Attribute extraction: inspect span/metric resource attributes and infer model properties (model_family, quantization, max_seq_bucket). 2) Compute low-cardinality tag 'model_shape' using a deterministic mapping (e.g., llama-7b|8k, gptx-13b|16k, custom-small). 3) Replace high-cardinality attributes with stable aggregates (sequence_length_bucket, prompt_signature_id hashed to 8 chars) and drop raw prompt text. 4) Optional sketching: for latency histograms, attach a tenant-aware sketch id to enable downstream rollups without exploding series. 5) Forward out to central OTLP endpoint and to a Prometheus remote_write adapter with configuration-driven label allowlist/denylist.

Design considerations: must be low-latency (<2ms p50 added), safe for PII (no raw text forwarded), opt-in per-namespace/tenant, feature-flagged and configurable via ConfigMap. Implementation will provide a compatibility shim so existing prometheus exporters can still receive original labels if downstream requests opt-in.

Telemetry & validation: add test harness that replays production traces against the preprocessor and measures series count reduction, remote_write throughput, and memory usage. Target: >=60% series reduction for high-cardinality tenants and <10% p95 added tail latency on request path.

Rollout plan: 1) Nightly integration tests + load bench in staging. 2) Canary in dev-region for low-traffic tenant group (2 weeks). 3) Open opt-in for tenants to trial (dashboard: Telemetry -> Cardinality Impact). 4) Gradual enablement (one region at a time) and monitoring of TSDB ingestion rates and query error rates.

Security & compliance: request security review for attribute redaction rules and KMS usage for stable hashing of tenant ids. Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TELEMETRY/edge-otlp-preprocessor
